# Quantum Channel Coherentization

Question: ordinary uses of an unknown unital quantum channel versus a coherent Liouville operator for spectral algorithms.

Story: README.md -> science/interpretation.md -> science/examples.md.
Exact assumptions and normalization: science/model.md.
Upper proof: science/collision-compiler.md; complete-unitary block output: science/block-encoding.md.
Lower proof: science/dimension-lower-bound.md. Its robust inversion reduction uses one forward compiled block and no compiler inverse.
Implementation: science/resources.md. Count channel calls, known gates, phase synthesis, disposable program and work qubits separately.
Prior work: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib.
Learning: learning/README.md; fixed project map: learning/MILESTONES.md; selected source and convention translation: learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md (John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, 2018).
Reproduction: verification/README.md, verification/verify.py, verification/report.json.

Essential distinctions: ordinary channel is the input; dilation/inverse/control are not supplied. All diamond norms are unhalved. The output target has no hidden dimension normalization; its exact designated block is Herm(L)/pi. Quadratic dimension order is matched at fixed precision, not a joint d-squared-over-error lower law. The ideal block ancilla count is constant; physical workspace is logarithmic in dimension. No application-level speedup is claimed.
